title: Describe a story and get the first draft
prompt:
# Story 2: Describe a story and get the first draft

- **Story**: XXX-describe-story
- **Created**: 2026-11-09
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: with the checkbox not ticked, write "As a returning customer, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that I can see my
  orders.", press Enter, and see the draft card with `stories/001-as-a-returning-customer-i/story.md` and the story appearing in it as it is written.

## Story

As a team member, I want to describe in my own words what a user needs, so that the AI drafts a user story with acceptance tests and tasks
that I can read as it is written.

## Acceptance tests

Sending

- [ ] **Given** the checkbox is not ticked and the box has text, **When** the user presses Enter (or the send button), **Then** the box is
  cleared, the text shows as a message on the right (as typed, with its line breaks), and a draft card appears under it.
- [ ] **Given** no text (or only spaces), **Then** the send button is disabled.
- [ ] **Given** the draft card, **Then** it shows the **story icon** (a document, in a blue tile), the planned path
  `stories/001-as-a-returning-customer-i/story.md` (complete as a tooltip), the chip "Writing...", and the text as it is written. It shows no
  chip of ADRs, because a story derives from none, and the chips of its links, if it has any (story 6).
- [ ] **Given** no model is connected, **When** the user sends, **Then** the draft fails with "No model is connected for this project. Connect
  one in Integrations." (`story-architectural-enablers.md`, story 2 shows how a failure looks).

The number and the name

- [ ] **Given** stories 001 and 002 exist, **Then** the planned number is `003`: the highest number of **all** the stories (inside a theme
  or not) plus one, with **3 digits** (`001` when there is none).
- [ ] **Given** the prompt "As a returning customer, I want to sign in with my email and password, so that I can see my orders.", **Then** the
  slug is `as-a-returning-customer-i`: the first five words, lower case, without accents, only `a-z` and `0-9` joined by "-", at most 48
  characters, and `untitled` when nothing is left. The folder is `001-as-a-returning-customer-i`.
- [ ] **Given** the identifier sent to the model, **Then** it is the folder name, `001-as-a-returning-customer-i`.
- [ ] **Given** two stories that start with the same words, **Then** their folders differ by their number.

The call

- [ ] **Given** the user sends, **Then** the browser calls only the BWYN backend, as `story-architectural-enablers.md` (story 1) describes, with
  the project, the system prompt, the context and the turns. It never calls the model's provider.
- [ ] **Given** the request, **Then** it says "Document type: user story", "Assigned identifier: 001-as-a-returning-customer-i", today's date,
  and the user's text under "Description". It has **no** "Derives from (ADRs)" section. Story 5 adds the project context and the lists of
  enablers and stories, and story 6 the linked documents.
- [ ] **Given** a new request while another is being written, **Then** the one in flight is cancelled.

What the draft is like (checked by reading drafts from a real model; they are not automated)

- [ ] **Given** a draft, **Then** it follows the template: `# Story: <short title>`, the lines Story (the identifier), Created (today's date) and
  Status (Draft), and the sections Story ("As a ..., I want ..., so that ..."), Acceptance tests, Business rules and constraints, Out of
  scope and Tasks.
- [ ] **Given** the acceptance tests, **Then** each is a Given, When and Then example with real values from the request, written as an unchecked
  box (`- [ ]`), never numbered and never checked.
- [ ] **Given** the Tasks, **Then** they are small engineering steps, one per line as an unchecked box, each starting with a verb, in the order
  they are done, covering the acceptance tests and nothing beyond them.
- [ ] **Given** a request that is bigger than one iteration of a pair, **Then** the draft holds the first and most valuable slice and names what
  it left out under Out of scope.
- [ ] **Given** a draft, **Then** it chooses no technology and no code structure, makes no estimate, uses the role from the request ("user"
  when there is none), and invents no facts: what is missing is the smallest reasonable assumption under Business rules and constraints.

## Business rules and constraints

- A story is **one Markdown file in its own folder**, `stories/<number>-<slug>/story.md`. The folder name is its identity, which never
  changes, and it is the base of every link to it (`story:001-as-a-returning-customer-i`).
- The number is the highest story number plus one, over all the stories. It is **3 digits** for a story and 4 for an enabler.
- The slug comes from the user's text when it is sent, so that the path is known and shown while the draft is written.
- The AI only drafts. Nothing is kept until the user approves (story 4).
- The model is asked for one Markdown document, with no introduction, no closing remark and no code fence.
- The same system prompt serves stories and enablers, with a template for each. The story rules are in the Reference.
- The keys of the model stay on the backend (`story-llm-provider.md`).

## Out of scope

- The state of the draft, Stop, Retry, Discard and the token counts (story 3), approving (story 4), the project context (story 5) and the
  links (story 6).
- The user story template as a file the team edits, a template per project, and several stories from one prompt.
- Where the story goes among themes: a new story starts **outside any theme** (`story-group-stories-by-theme.md`).

## Tasks

- [ ] Choose the next story number (three digits, over every story, in or out of a theme) and the slug, and set the planned path
  `stories/<number>-<slug>/story.md` and the identifier.
- [ ] Write the story part of the system prompt (the rules and the template of the Reference) and split the rules from the enabler's (see
  `story-architectural-enablers.md`, story 5).
- [ ] Build the request text for a story: "Document type: user story", the identifier, the date and the description, with no "Derives from".
- [ ] Start the draft in create mode for a story, and show its card with the story icon and path.
- [ ] Test with a fake backend: the number with and without themes, the slug, the identifier, and the request that is sent.

tasks.text: Implement the story-number calculation: query all existing stories (in and out of themes), find the highest number, add one, and zero-pad to three digits.
Implement slug generation from the prompt: take the first five words, lower-case, strip accents, keep only `a-z0-9`, join with `-`, truncate to 48 characters, fall back to `untitled`.
Compose the planned path `stories/<number>-<slug>/story.md` and the identifier `<number>-<slug>` as soon as the user sends.
Write the story section of the system prompt (rules and template) and split it from the enabler section so each document type uses its own template.
Build the request body for a story: "Document type: user story", the identifier, today's date, and the user's description; omit the "Derives from (ADRs)" section.
Wire the send action: clear the prompt box, display the user message on the right, open the draft card with the story icon (blue tile), the planned path as a tooltip, and the "Writing…" chip.
Stream the model response into the draft card text area, cancelling any in-flight request when a new one starts.
Show the failure message "No model is connected for this project. Connect one in Integrations." in the draft card when no model is configured.
Disable the send button when the prompt box is empty or contains only whitespace.
Write unit tests with a fake backend covering: number calculation with and without themes, slug generation edge cases, identifier composition, and the exact request body sent to the backend.
